Feiyin Tongrong owns the retained address: the whole device unfolds, one way held up, covering the old and outdoing the new, overleaping sound and color — the heads of the recompense and transformation bodies thrust out, the nostrils of the birth-mother pulled free; discern the mark here and you can deploy the great device and issue the great use — breaking chains and locks with the iron-browed, crushing bone and taking marrow with the exceptional-eyed, loosening the stuck in heaven and among men, drawing nails and pulling wedges in the field of the buddhas and patriarchs. That is why it is said: unobstructed across and athwart, free in killing and giving life, I am the king of the teaching, at ease in the teaching. Just at such a moment — what is the one sentence that settles the house and fixes the estate? The staff lifted and pressed on the knee: the Moye held crosswise, the full true command; the peaceful world beheads the dull and stubborn.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J27/J27nB193.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yinyuan. Yinyuan Longqi owns the retained address: that is why our Linji, seeing a monk enter the gate, cried out, and Deshan, seeing a monk enter the gate, took the rod — and: the true student does not shrink from losing his body and his life; at Huangbo I three times asked the great intent of the Buddha's teaching and three times took a painful beating, like wormwood brush flicking past; even now I long for one more taste, but no one dares strike. A monk said: I will strike. Linji handed him the rod; as the monk reached to take it, Linji struck. Look at this old fellow's working — like wind turning back into fire, like a galloping current crossing a blade: poison within poison, edge upon edge, teeth growing on teeth, horns growing on horns, free in killing and giving life, blazing through a thousand ages. Whoever inherits his lineage must understand its purport — how could babbling kindness, clinking little virtue, twittering words, and trifling conduct mix in and stain the outline handed down from of old? Now is the summer-session season; the assembly has asked me to ascend this seat and unfold the treasury of the true eye, point by point setting out right knowing and right seeing in the pure great perfect awakening, for all to share. Do you all fully grasp it or not? Swept clear the stench ten thousand li; only the true vein flows on forever. And he descended.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J26/J26nB182.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Wanru. Wanru Tongwei owns the retained address: the true eye, pierced through without remainder; the wondrous pure bright mind, outdoing today and surpassing the old; wide as the great void, bright as the noon sun, blazing in the open — even the wise go astray; a blade hidden in the sleeve, the adept at a loss; nakedly clean, beyond taking up; bare and dripping, beyond grasping. Hence it is said: always within activity, and within activity not gathered in. Arrived here — does it admit the three mysteries and five positions? does it admit the black-and-white circle? does it admit the one word with three sentences? does it admit the six attributes and ten mysteries? Admitting none of them, what is prized is only cutting straight through and sitting it down, silent, knowing the return. Like night-pearl in the dish, slantwise beyond measuring; the Tai'e in the grip, free in killing and giving life. Tell me: what is the one sentence that wins the marvel while following the stream? — a white egret into the field, a thousand flecks of snow; an oriole up the tree, one branch of flowers.

Ruibai Mingxue owns the retained letter, written from Bian Mountain in reply to the scholar Yan Jiyu: your letter received — I know the layman's spirit towers and his edge is keen, truly like a seasoned general with the bearing of one who receives enemies on eight sides. But not yet long seasoned in the line of battle, should he meet the strong of the strong and the best of the best, I fear he will be seized alive and taken captive — and the face would not be pretty. Better only to store deep and nurture full: when stray thoughts are exhausted and prajna is round and bright, then come forward — one rod, one stripe of scar; one palm, one handful of blood; free in killing and giving life, at ease in gathering and releasing — would that not be a joy!

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J36/J36nB369.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Zhe'an Fan. Zhe'an Jingfan owns the retained address, asking the fellow-monks of the two ranks to the hall: one embroidered garment is no fine sight; a single-stringed zither hardly stirs the ear — it takes those of the same breath seeking each other and the same voice answering, the honored bending to the humble, drumming wide the teaching's transformation, near and far made one, new and old both forgotten, inner and outer solemn, commands stern. Use Muzhou's heart-conduct to spur those beaten on the Hutuo; hold up Gao'an's bearing to scold Fojian's pickled greens. Beat Yangqi's drum, press Ciming's evening hall; let loose Xuedou's eloquence, entertain Taiyang's fine guest. Baoshou's raw ginger, sharp to the very last; Guishan's kitchen knife, free in killing and giving life. Even should a hero arrive, he will know this gate stands high — he may pick up a hint at most from the attendant's side. Thus can the true eye of heaven and humankind be widened, the hidden device of the buddhas and patriarchs broadcast, an unfading estate of the grove built, and the downward-rushing billows of the Long River stemmed. I dare pledge: King Shengyin never saw such a deed — how would the teacher Vairocana know this style of rule? Summoning the assembly: tell me — according to what is there such wonder?
